title: Sleep and memory
text: Getting seven to nine hours of rest each night helps the brain consolidate memories. Students who stay up all night before exams often remember less, not more.

title: Hydration
text: Drinking enough water keeps your body temperature stable and your joints lubricated. Mild dehydration can cause headaches, tiredness and poor concentration.

title: The common cold
text: Colds are caused by viruses, so antibiotics do not cure them. Rest, fluids and time are usually the best treatment.

title: Exercise and mood
text: Regular physical activity releases endorphins that lift your mood. Even a brisk thirty-minute walk can reduce feelings of anxiety and stress.

title: Sugar and teeth
text: Bacteria in the mouth feed on sugar and produce acids that damage tooth enamel. Brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste prevents cavities.

title: Vitamin D
text: The skin produces vitamin D when exposed to sunlight. A deficiency can weaken bones and is common in people who spend most of their time indoors.

title: Blood pressure
text: Eating too much salt can raise blood pressure over time. Hypertension increases the risk of heart attacks and strokes.

title: Screens and eye strain
text: Staring at a monitor for hours can cause dry, strained eyes. The 20-20-20 rule suggests looking 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes.

title: How vaccines work
text: Vaccines train the immune system to recognise a germ without causing the disease. This is how smallpox was eliminated worldwide.

title: Meditation
text: Mindfulness meditation teaches you to focus on your breathing and observe thoughts calmly. Studies link it with lower stress and better attention.

title: Password security
text: Long passphrases are harder to crack than short complex passwords. Enabling two-factor authentication adds a second layer of protection to your accounts.

title: How Wi-Fi works
text: A wireless router sends data using radio waves. Thick walls and microwave ovens can weaken the signal and slow your connection.

title: Smartphone battery
text: Lithium-ion batteries slowly lose capacity with every charge cycle. Avoiding extreme heat helps your phone battery last longer.

title: Cloud storage
text: Cloud services store your files on remote servers so you can access them from any device. Backing up photos online protects them if your laptop is lost.

title: Machine learning
text: Machine learning lets computers learn patterns from examples instead of following hand-written rules. Email filters learn to recognise junk messages this way.

title: Phishing scams
text: Phishing emails pretend to come from a bank or company to trick you into revealing your login details. Always check the sender's address before clicking a link.

title: Electric cars
text: Electric vehicles run on battery-powered motors and produce no tailpipe emissions. Charging at home overnight is cheaper than buying petrol.

title: Sluggish computers
text: A computer becomes sluggish when too many programs run at startup or the disk is almost full. Uninstalling unused apps often makes it faster.

title: Open-source software
text: Open-source software publishes its code so anyone can read, modify and share it. Linux and Python are famous examples.

title: Quantum computing
text: Quantum computers use qubits that can represent zero and one at the same time. They may one day solve problems that are impossible for ordinary computers.

title: Black holes
text: A black hole is a region where gravity is so strong that not even light can escape. They form when massive stars collapse at the end of their lives.

title: Mars
text: Mars is called the red planet because its soil is rich in iron oxide, which is rust. Robotic rovers are searching it for signs of ancient life.

title: Phases of the Moon
text: The Moon does not produce its own light; we see sunlight reflecting off it. Its shape seems to change during the month as its position around Earth changes.

title: The space station
text: The International Space Station circles Earth about sixteen times a day. Crew members on board conduct experiments in near weightlessness.

title: The Sun
text: The Sun is a star powered by nuclear fusion, turning hydrogen into helium in its core. Its light takes about eight minutes to reach Earth.

title: Exoplanets
text: Astronomers have discovered thousands of planets orbiting other stars. Some lie in the habitable zone where liquid water could exist.

title: Asteroids
text: Most asteroids orbit the Sun in a belt between Mars and Jupiter. An asteroid impact is believed to have wiped out the dinosaurs.

title: Why we have seasons
text: Earth has seasons because its axis is tilted, not because its distance from the Sun changes. Summer happens when your hemisphere leans toward the Sun.

title: Space telescopes
text: The James Webb Space Telescope observes infrared light, letting it see the very first galaxies. It sits far beyond the Moon to stay cold.

title: Rockets
text: Rockets push hot gas out of their engines, and the reaction drives them upward. Reusable boosters that land themselves have made launches cheaper.

title: Baking bread
text: Yeast eats sugar in the dough and releases carbon dioxide, which makes bread rise. Kneading builds gluten that gives the loaf its chewy texture.

title: Spicy food
text: Chilli peppers contain capsaicin, which triggers heat sensors on your tongue. Milk soothes the burning better than water.

title: Coffee and caffeine
text: Caffeine blocks a brain chemical called adenosine that makes you feel drowsy. Drinking it late in the day can disturb your night's rest.

title: Preserving food
text: Freezing, salting and drying slow down the bacteria that spoil food. Pickling in vinegar creates an acidic environment where germs cannot grow.

title: Protein sources
text: Lentils, beans, eggs and paneer are good sources of protein. Muscles need protein to repair themselves after a workout.

title: Cooking rice
text: Rinsing rice removes extra starch so the grains stay separate. A ratio of roughly two cups of water to one cup of rice works for most varieties.

title: Chocolate
text: Chocolate is made from fermented and roasted cacao beans. Dark chocolate contains more cocoa and less sugar than milk chocolate.

title: Onions and tears
text: Cutting an onion releases a gas that irritates the eyes and makes them water. Chilling the onion first reduces the effect.

title: Fermented foods
text: Yogurt, idli batter and kimchi are made by friendly microbes that ferment food. These probiotics may support healthy digestion.

title: Avocados
text: Avocados are rich in healthy fats and fibre. They ripen faster when stored in a paper bag with a banana.

title: Jet lag
text: Flying across several time zones confuses your body clock. Getting morning sunlight at your destination helps you adjust faster.

title: Packing light
text: Rolling garments instead of folding them saves space in a suitcase. Carrying only hand luggage avoids waiting at baggage claim.

title: Travel insurance
text: Travel insurance covers unexpected costs such as medical emergencies abroad or cancelled flights. It is cheap compared to a hospital bill in a foreign country.

title: Passports and visas
text: Many countries require your passport to be valid for at least six months after arrival. Check the visa rules well before booking tickets.

title: Cheap flights
text: Airfares are often lower when booked several weeks in advance and for mid-week departures. Flexible dates can save a lot of money.

title: Motion sickness
text: Nausea on boats or in cars happens when your eyes and inner ear send conflicting signals. Looking at the horizon can ease the queasy feeling.

title: Solo travel
text: Travelling alone lets you set your own schedule and meet new people. Share your itinerary with family for safety.

title: Respecting local culture
text: Learning a few words of the local language shows respect. Research customs such as dress codes before visiting religious sites.

title: Hill stations
text: Hill stations like Ooty, Munnar and Shimla offer cool weather in summer. They were popular retreats during the hot months.

title: Train journeys
text: Long-distance trains let you watch the countryside go by and are often greener than flying. Sleeper berths make overnight trips comfortable.

title: Compound interest
text: Compound interest means you earn interest on your interest. Starting early lets your savings grow much larger over time.

title: Budgeting
text: The 50-30-20 rule splits income into needs, wants and savings. Tracking every expense for a month reveals where money disappears.

title: Emergency fund
text: An emergency fund covers three to six months of living expenses. It protects you if you suddenly lose your job.

title: Credit score
text: Paying bills on time and keeping card balances low improves your credit score. A good score makes loans cheaper.

title: Inflation
text: Inflation means prices rise over time, so the same money buys less. Cash kept under a mattress quietly loses value.

title: Stocks and shares
text: Buying a share makes you a part-owner of a company. Share prices go up and down, so investing for the long term reduces risk.

title: Diversification
text: Diversification means spreading your money across many investments. If one fails, the others cushion the loss, so don't put all your eggs in one basket.

title: Income tax
text: Income tax is collected by the government to fund roads, schools and hospitals. Investments in certain schemes can reduce how much tax you owe.

title: Cryptocurrency
text: Bitcoin is a digital currency recorded on a public ledger called a blockchain. Its price is extremely volatile.

title: Loans and EMI
text: An EMI is a fixed monthly payment that repays a loan with interest. A longer loan term lowers the EMI but increases the total interest paid.

title: Cricket
text: In cricket, a batter scores a six by hitting the ball over the boundary without it bouncing. A team has eleven players.

title: Football
text: Football is the world's most popular sport, played by two teams trying to kick the ball into the opponent's goal. The FIFA World Cup is held every four years.

title: The Olympics
text: The modern Olympic Games began in Athens in 1896. Athletes compete for gold, silver and bronze medals.

title: Marathons
text: A marathon is a race of 42.195 kilometres on foot. Runners train for months, gradually increasing their weekly distance.

title: Chess
text: Chess is a strategy board game where each player tries to checkmate the opponent's king. Grandmasters calculate many moves ahead.

title: Warming up
text: Warming up before sport increases blood flow to muscles and reduces the chance of injury. Dynamic stretches like leg swings work well.

title: Tennis
text: Tennis matches are scored using points called love, fifteen, thirty and forty. Wimbledon is played on grass courts.

title: Badminton
text: The shuttlecock in badminton can travel faster than 400 kilometres per hour in a smash. It is one of the fastest racket sports.

title: Swimming
text: Swimming works almost every muscle in the body while being gentle on the joints. It is often recommended for people recovering from injuries.

title: Yoga
text: Yoga combines physical postures, breathing and relaxation. It improves flexibility and balance.

title: Climate change
text: Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide that traps heat in the atmosphere. This is warming the planet and melting glaciers.

title: Recycling
text: Recycling turns used paper, glass and metal into new products. It saves energy and keeps waste out of landfills.

title: Plastic in the ocean
text: Millions of tonnes of plastic end up in the sea every year. Turtles and seabirds mistake plastic bags for food.

title: Solar power
text: Solar panels convert sunlight directly into electricity. Prices have fallen so much that solar is now one of the cheapest energy sources.

title: Deforestation
text: Cutting down forests destroys the homes of countless animals and plants. Trees also absorb carbon dioxide, so losing them speeds up global warming.

title: Air pollution
text: Smoke from vehicles, factories and crop burning fills cities with tiny harmful particles. Breathing polluted air damages the lungs.

title: Saving water
text: Fixing leaking taps and taking shorter showers saves thousands of litres a year. Rainwater harvesting collects rain for later use.

title: Bees in decline
text: Bees pollinate many of the crops we eat. Pesticides and habitat loss are causing their numbers to fall.

title: Composting
text: Kitchen scraps like vegetable peels can be composted into rich soil. This reduces garbage and feeds garden plants naturally.

title: Endangered species
text: Tigers, rhinos and snow leopards are endangered due to hunting and habitat loss. Protected reserves help their populations recover.
